opening_message:
Ticket 1: Christopher Myers (employee ID E012) requests write access to Source Code.

Team memory: 2 note(s) about employee E012.
Note 1 (ticket 1):
  - role: Analyst
  - employment type: full_time
  - recommendation for Source Code: write
  - comment: Christopher Myers (E012) is a full-time Analyst requesting write access to Source Code. As a full-time employee, the maximum access is write (admin requires the role to own the system; Analyst does not own Source Code). The requested write level is within policy, so recommend write.
Note 2 (ticket 1):
  - employment type: contractor
  - security training: basic
  - recommendation for Source Code: read
  - comment: Security DB shows Christopher Myers (E012) is a contractor with basic security training, not full-time. Contractors with basic training max out at read access; admin is never allowed. Requested write is above the maximum, so recommend read.
reason: There is a conflict between the two notes: HR indicates E012 is a full-time Analyst (max write), while Security DB indicates E012 is a contractor with basic security training (max read; write requires advanced training). Given the conflicting employment-type facts and the Security record showing only basic training, the safe decision that complies with policy is read, which is within policy under either interpretation and does not exceed the requested write level.
